rows: A deficit that the government plans to increase by borrowing from private savers

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the loanable funds market in Bayland, labeling the equilibrium real interest rate r1. Then show the effect of the government's increased borrowing on your graph and label the new real interest rate r2.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Downward-sloping demand and upward-sloping supply of loanable funds with the real interest rate on the vertical axis; demand shifts right and the new real interest rate r2 is above r1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Loanable funds graph labeled
required_elements: Draws a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve for loanable funds, labels the vertical axis the real interest rate and the horizontal axis the quantity of loanable funds, and labels the equilibrium real interest rate r1
alt_solutions: curves may be labeled D and S
axis may say interest rate or price of loanable funds
common_errors: labels the vertical axis as the nominal interest rate
draws the supply curve downward sloping
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Demand shifts right; r2 higher
required_elements: Shifts the demand curve for loanable funds to the right and labels a new real interest rate r2 above r1
alt_solutions: draws and labels D2
dashed line to r2 at the new intersection
common_errors: shifts the supply curve to the right
labels r2 below r1
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the effect of the government's increased borrowing on private investment spending, and explain.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Private investment spending decreases (crowding out), because the higher real interest rate makes borrowing more expensive and fewer investment projects are profitable.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the reason: private investment decreases
required_elements: States that private investment spending decreases (crowding out)
alt_solutions: private investment falls
a correct equivalent statement in the student's own words
common_errors: says private investment increases
says investment is unchanged
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the reason: higher real rate reduces investment
required_elements: Explains that the higher real interest rate raises the cost of borrowing, so firms undertake less investment
alt_solutions: fewer projects have returns above the cost of funds
a correct equivalent statement in the student's own words
common_errors: says the lower real interest rate reduces investment
says firms have less income
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Explain how this change in private investment affects the economy's long-run growth.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Less private investment slows the growth of the capital stock, so potential output and long-run aggregate supply grow more slowly.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the reason: slower capital accumulation lowers growth
required_elements: Explains that lower investment reduces the growth of the capital stock, so long-run aggregate supply (potential output) grows more slowly
alt_solutions: a smaller capital stock lowers productivity growth
a correct equivalent statement in the student's own words
common_errors: says long-run growth is unaffected by investment
says growth speeds up
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.
